answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small, time-bound stake before it can transact, with the stake growing as honest reputation accrues. Like a zephyr bending a willow without breaking it, genuine participation flexes and recovers, while a flood of fake identities faces real cost. One bad actor's ripple of sock-puppet accounts then costs more than it gains, because misbehavior burns the stake behind each identity.
